proposed_extended_aspects.difficulty: Conceptual or technical challenge of the course.
proposed_extended_aspects.clarity: How understandable the teaching and explanations feel.
proposed_extended_aspects.workload: Amount of sustained effort required across the term.
proposed_extended_aspects.lecturer_quality: Perceived quality of the lecturer or lead instructor.
proposed_extended_aspects.exam_fairness: Whether exams feel aligned and fair.
proposed_extended_aspects.relevance: Perceived usefulness to the program or future goals.
proposed_extended_aspects.interest: Level of engagement or curiosity the course creates.
proposed_extended_aspects.support: Quality of help from instructor, TAs, or forums.
proposed_extended_aspects.materials: Usefulness of slides, notes, readings, and resources.
proposed_extended_aspects.feedback_quality: Usefulness and timeliness of feedback on student work.
proposed_extended_aspects.assessment_design: Alignment and structure of assignments, projects, and exams.
proposed_extended_aspects.pacing: Whether the course tempo and weekly rhythm are manageable.
proposed_extended_aspects.organization: Administrative clarity, course structure, and coordination.
proposed_extended_aspects.practical_application: Connection to real-world practice or authentic tasks.
proposed_extended_aspects.tooling_usability: Friction or support created by LMS, submission systems, and required software.
proposed_extended_aspects.accessibility: Perceived accessibility and inclusiveness of materials, pace, and course participation.
proposed_extended_aspects.grading_transparency: How clearly grading criteria, rubrics, and score interpretation are communicated.
proposed_extended_aspects.peer_interaction: Whether peer discussion, teamwork, and class community help or hinder learning.
proposed_extended_aspects.prerequisite_fit: How well the course matches the advertised prerequisite level and student preparation.

recommended_sampling_rule.aspect_count: Sample 1, 2, or 3 aspects using the fixed binary-polarity distribution for the new generation cycle.

diversity_strengths: The schema now varies student background, motivation, assessment structure, support experience, hedging, contradiction patterns, and recommendation stance.
The sampled attributes create broader lexical and situational diversity than style plus grade alone.
Only a subset of nuance attributes is surfaced per prompt so reviews do not read like exhaustive templates.
realism_strengths: The schema includes grounded friction, time pressure, and contradiction patterns that mimic real student reviews.
The prompt explicitly discourages checklist structure and over-balanced summaries.
aspect_extension_rationale: The proposed next-generation inventory separates feedback quality, pacing, organization, assessment design, tooling usability, accessibility, grading transparency, peer interaction, and prerequisite fit from generic overall experience.
Those extra aspects are pedagogically actionable and reduce the collapse of distinct student concerns into a single broad sentiment label.
remaining_risks: Without live OpenAI prompt-debug cycles, some attribute combinations may still generate overly tidy reviews.
Human validation and synthetic-vs-real discrimination remain necessary for external realism claims.
